2. Sonali Bank Limited filed the aforesaid suit for decree of Taka 3,91,05,805/28and in that suit,originally i.e. the Company as well as Managing Director was made party. The suit was decreed and subsequently decree was put into execution. Defendant Nos. 3 and 5, who was impleaded as director of the Company, filed application for striking out their names from original proceeding. By the impugned order learned Judge strikeout the name of defendant Nos.3 and 5 from execution proceeding. 

 3. Mr Mohammad Eunus, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner, submits that; after contested hearing the suit was decreed and decree was put into execution against defendants who are legally directors and it is settled principle of law that executing court cannot go beyond the decree as such the learned Judge committed gross illegality in striking out the name of defendant Nos. 3 and 5 from execution proceeding. 

 12. Sub-section 5 of section 6 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 made provision as to against whom the suit can be filed for realization of money. This law yeardstick that the suit can be filed against principal debtor, then 3rd party mortgagor and 3 party guarantor. But in presence of principal debtor, 3rd party mortgagor or 3rd party guarantor may not took party in the proceeding as they are impleaded in the case if principal debtor failed to satisfy the decree, money is to be realised from these 3rdpartys, as per law. A common duty cast upon on the financial institutions in executing the decree that they are disbursing public money and if it is found that decree cannot be satisfied against principal debtor and also 3rdparty mortgagor or 3rd party guarantor, then the decree must be satisfied from Bank's officials who are involved in the transaction granting loan. Law does not say any of the official of the principal debtor can be impleaded in the suit and if that be impleaded in the suit, either on the application of the financial institution or suo motu by court then a step has been taken outside law. If neither of the parties as aforesaid satisfy the decree, then financial institutions/banks can go for realising money from the share holders of the principal debtors in civil court by filing money suit as law does not permit to file any suit under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 against those persons other than the 3 categories mention in section 6 Sub-section 5 of the Act. 

 17. Now, let us consider-whether Artha Rin Adalat is a Civil Court in executing decree. Section 6(1) of the Ain is as follows: 

 18. On a reading of section 6(1) of the Ain it appears that in executing the decree Artha Rin Adalat follows the procedure laid down in Code of Civil Procedure and it is settled executing court cannot go beyond the decree. 

 20. Collective reading of the above quoted sections shows that Artha Rin Adalat shall follow and apply the Code of Civil Procedure as a Civil Court in exercising its jurisdiction, powers and functions while adjudicating any dispute between the parties before it including execution of its decree insofar as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of section 6(Ka) or any other provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. Section 6(Ka), in our view, has excluded the operation of Rules 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 in matters of execution of any decree. In order words, Artha Rin Adalat shall execute its decree applying the provisions of sections 55 and 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Order XXI and the rules made thereunder except the rules 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9. Application of section 56 of the Code, in our view, has not been excluded by section 6(Ka).
